conviction_note: The findings roughly offset (impact_sum -0.4). Positives: a beat-the-guide pattern, peers' PC margins holding after HP last spoke, PC DRAM inflation slowing, and a crowded put skew. Negatives: HP's calendar-Q3 units fell 31%, finished goods are piling up in North American channels, the 2027 unit outlook has darkened since HP's 21 Sep assumption, an interim team sets the FY27 guide before a new CEO arrives, and Xerox cut its print outlook. So p_up sits at 49 on an 8.0% abs move (option-implied 8.24%), giving -0.16. The two numbers agree in sign and size.
bar: Q4 FY26 non-GAAP EPS. Company guide: $0.69-0.79, including $0.08 of estimated tariff refunds (Q3 FY26 call, 2026-08-26, https://s203.q4cdn.com/918857832/files/content_files/Q3-2026_HP-Inc_Earnings-Transcript.pdf). Consensus: $0.75 EPS on $15.47B revenue, with a whisper of $0.90 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16, https://finviz.com/news/423393/hps-memory-cost-trough-meets-a-whisper-number-above-its-own-guidance; that article also misquotes the guide using the GAAP range of $0.74-0.84). The quarter bar is anchored by the company guide. The real bar is FY27 EPS. The only consensus found is $2.90-2.93, and it is stale (Barchart, April 2026 and pre-Q3: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-hp-inc-next-quarterly-124047736.html). For comparison, FY26 guidance is $3.19-3.29, or about $3.00-3.10 excluding $0.19 of tariff refunds. Because the FY27 bar is unsourced to current estimates, every guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest: 76.42M shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, about 8.5% of the 901.8M shares outstanding, 5.91 days to cover. It has edged up from 73.09M (4.60 days) on 2026-09-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/hpq/short-interest). That is elevated for a mega-cap but not squeeze territory (under 10%). The 25-delta skew is +7.58 vol points, so downside is bid. Put/call OI is 0.67. The event-implied move is 8.24%, against a median of 3.62% and a maximum of 8.27% over the last 8 prints. The stock is -15.31% over 20 days and -19.84% from its 52-week high, after a six-session 17.1% slide to $28.27 on 2026-11-03 that had no company cause (Trefis, https://www.trefis.com/stock/hpq/articles/622463/6-red-days-in-a-row-hp-stock-is-down-17/2026-11-04). Analysts: 15 covering, 1 Strong Buy / 9 Hold / 1 Moderate Sell / 4 Strong Sell (Barchart, April 2026). Morgan Stanley has been Underweight since Nov 2025.

findings.finding: HP has beaten its own guide three quarters running. Q3 FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $0.83 against a $0.61-0.71 guide, and still above the top at about $0.72 excluding the $0.11 tariff refund. Q4 consensus of $0.75 sits in the lower half of the $0.69-0.79 guide, while the whisper is $0.90. A Q4 print around $0.80 or more (about +5-7% vs $0.75) is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q3 FY26 (2026-08-26): EPS above the top of the guide and the FY guide raised, but the stock fell 2.92% (invezz: 'HP stock slides 5% as memory costs pressure PC margins'). Q2 FY26: -1.88%. Only 3 of the last 8 prints were up.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.75 is $0.04 below the guide midpoint, even though HP has cleared the top of its range repeatedly. If the market had priced the habit, consensus would sit at or above the $0.74 midpoint. The $0.90 whisper shows part of the buy side does expect it, so this is partly priced.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview with consensus $0.75 vs whisper $0.90 (https://finviz.com/news/423393/hps-memory-cost-trough-meets-a-whisper-number-above-its-own-guidance). Same quarter, different source.

findings.finding: On IDC's count, HP's calendar-Q3 (Jul-Sep) shipments fell 30.9% YoY to 10.3M, and its share fell from 19.1% to 16.5%. That is worse than the market (-20.1%), Lenovo (-22.6%) and Dell (-25%), and far worse than the -16% units HP itself reported for May-Jul. Consensus revenue of $15.47B, with Print near $4.2B, implies Personal Systems of about $11.3B (about +8-9% YoY on Q4 FY25's $10.4B). At -30% units that needs ASPs up roughly 55%, against about +40% in Q3, so there is risk to PS revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PS revenue has beaten every quarter this year, and the stock still fell on margin (Aug 2026, -2.92%). The stock fell about 7% on 2026-10-09 when the IDC/Gartner data came out (tradingkey market movers, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262209175-market-movers-hpq-20261009).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 8-12 October, and the stock already reacted (-7% on 10-09), so it is largely priced. What may not be priced is the arithmetic against consensus PS revenue: the $15.47B consensus still implies high-single-digit PS growth. Units are a third-party proxy, and HP prioritises profitable units, so this matters more for revenue than for EPS.
findings.independence: Gartner gives the same HP -30.9% (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps), not independent of the unit read. HP's own Q4 FY25 segment base of PS $10.4B / Print $4.3B is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/47217/000004721725000068/hp103125exhibit991q425.htm.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after HP last spoke kept PC margins well above HP's 4.6% PS margin despite memory costs. Lenovo IDG (Jul-Sep, reported 2026-11-19): revenue +15% to $17.4B at a 7.1% operating margin, 'well maintained', even though Lenovo units fell 22.6%. Dell CSG (May-Jul, reported 2026-09-01): revenue +20% at 7.6%, up from 6.4% YoY. Pricing pass-through is working industry-wide, which supports HP's claim that Q4 is the PS margin trough before a recovery in FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PS margin is the line HP has traded on: the 4.6% PS margin in Q3 FY26 produced -2.92% despite an EPS beat. There is no clean record of an upside PS-margin surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: HP's stock has fallen 15% in 20 days, and the skew is +7.6, which prices a deeper or longer squeeze. A market that had absorbed Lenovo's held margin would not have kept HP near its lows through 11-19 to 11-24. Note that HP's gap to peers is partly HP-specific (consumer mix), so the read-across is partial.
findings.independence: Dell Q2 FY27 8-K exhibit, a different company and document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571996/000157199626000039/exhibit991earnings8kq2fy27.htm

findings.finding: PC memory inflation is slowing. TrendForce (2026-11-11) forecasts 4Q26 PC DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ, down from 18-23% in 3Q26, and client SSD up less than 5% QoQ. Suppliers have 'some room to moderate price increases'. This fits HP CFO Parkhill's FY27 frame that input costs keep rising 'at a slower rate than we have experienced in fiscal 2026'. Against it, Korean suppliers plan to cut PC DRAM supply in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Memory cost commentary drove the Feb 2026 print (-6% after hours on 'memory crunch will linger', per thestar.com.my 2026-02-25) and the Aug 2026 print (-2.92%).
findings.why_not_priced: The sell side's FY27 caution (Morgan Stanley Underweight, 4 Strong Sells) is built on unabated memory inflation, and the skew prices downside. If the deceleration were priced, the FY27 guide would be the upside risk rather than the feared one. Still a +13-18% quarterly rise, so this is a slowdown in the headwind, not its end.
findings.independence: HP Q3 FY26 call, CFO: 'input costs to continue to rise but at a slower rate' (https://s203.q4cdn.com/918857832/files/content_files/Q3-2026_HP-Inc_Earnings-Transcript.pdf), a company statement, not independent data.

findings.finding: The same TrendForce release reports finished-goods inventories rising in North American distribution channels and PC brands broadly cutting 4Q26 SSD purchases and revising 1Q27 plans down. Notebook shipments fell 15.8% QoQ in 3Q26, with a further single-digit decline possible in 4Q26. That is a weak setup for HP's Q1 FY27 (Nov-Jan) sell-in in the Americas, where HP has regained share leadership.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A soft next-period guide drove the Nov 2025 print (-1.4%, FY26 EPS forecast below the Street) and the Feb 2026 print (about -6% after hours). Negative guides have produced moderate, not extreme, declines.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it agrees with the +7.6 skew and the 20-day slide. HP said in August that channel inventory was 'higher than normal' but 'well controlled'. A North American channel build since then is new information about the quarter HP will guide.
findings.independence: Shares one document with the memory-slowdown finding, but reads a different fact (inventory, not price). IDC: 'Channels are now worried about carrying too much inventory' (https://computerworld.com/article/4233827/pc-prices-to-remain-elevated-until-end-of-2027.html, 2026-10-12).

findings.finding: HP's 8-K of 2026-09-21 set its FY27 planning assumption: industry PC units down roughly mid-single digits in calendar 2027, 'matching third-party forecasts' and dependent on a 'fluid' second half of 2026. Since then, the 2H26 data came in at -20% to -22% for calendar Q3, and IDC says the outlook 'gets worse before it gets better' and 'could deteriorate' into 2027. If HP lowers that assumption, the FY27 revenue base is cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 21 Sep 8-K itself moved the stock about -2% (finviz, https://finviz.com/news/393837/hp-shares-fall-2-as-company-anticipates-pc-market-contraction-in-2027).
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates anchored on the -MSD assumption would carry FY27 revenue near flat. A deeper unit assumption would show up as a lower FY27 bar, which the stale $2.90-2.93 consensus does not reflect. It agrees with the skew, so it is partly priced.
findings.independence: IDC 3Q26 release (https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26), a proxy; it shares the IDC document with the unit-decline finding.

findings.finding: HP named former GSK CEO Emma Walmsley as CEO effective 2027-01-04 (8-K of 2026-11-04). The FY27 guide will therefore come from an interim CEO (Broussard) and CFO Parkhill two months before a new CEO who has not yet set strategy, which raises the odds of a conservative or partial FY27 framework.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior HP print guided by an outgoing interim team. The Feb 2026 CEO change (Lores to PayPal) coincided with Q1 commentary; that print was +4.32% on 2026-02-03 (when Q1 was reaffirmed) and 0.05% on 2026-02-24.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is public. Its effect on how the guide is framed is inference, so this is sized small. If priced as a reset risk, the implied move would be elevated, and it is (8.24% vs a 3.62% median), so it is largely priced.
findings.independence: engineering.com coverage of the same announcement (https://www.engineering.com/hp-appoints-former-gsk-ceo-emma-walmsley-as-ceo/); same event, not independent.

findings.finding: Xerox, an office-print peer, cut its full-year adjusted operating income and FCF guidance on 2026-10-29, citing headwinds that 'intensified', 'higher costs, geopolitical uncertainty and competing IT priorities'. Its stock fell about 14% on the day. HP Print Commercial was already -1% with soft North American office demand in Q3, and Print is about 27% of HP revenue at an 18% margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Print has not been the line HP trades on this year. HP guided Q4 Print revenue to normal seasonality and margins to the lower half of 16-19% excluding refunds.
findings.why_not_priced: HP's six-day slide began around the same week, so this is likely partly in the price. Xerox is levered, lost share and is in an integration, so its read-across to HP is weak and this is sized small.
findings.independence: StockStory on the Xerox Q3 2026 reaction (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/xrx/news/earnings/xerox-nasdaqxrx-posts-q3-2026-sales-in-line-with-estimates-but-stock-drops-142percent); same event.

findings.finding: Positioning leans to downside going in. The 25-delta skew is +7.58 vol points. The event-implied move of 8.24% is 2.3x the median realised reaction of 3.62% and at the 8-print maximum of 8.27%. Short interest rose to 76.4M shares (about 8.5% of shares outstanding, 5.9 days to cover) by 2026-10-30. The stock lost 17.1% in six sessions to 2026-11-03 with no company news, while the S&P fell 1.4%. A guide that merely confirms the 'Q4 is the trough' frame meets a market positioned for worse.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: a soft FY26 guide into a weak tape produced only -1.4%. HP's last 8 reactions never exceeded 8.27% in either direction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The argument is that the options market's 8.24% event move and its put skew price a tail larger than any HP print in two years. The option market is right if the FY27 guide is a reset (new CEO, units). The absence of a cause for the slide is weak evidence, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Trefis on the six-day slide with no company cause (https://www.trefis.com/stock/hpq/articles/622463/6-red-days-in-a-row-hp-stock-is-down-17/2026-11-04); the sealed baseline gives the skew and implied move.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide includes $0.19 of tariff refunds ($0.08 in Q4). FY27 has no stated refund, so the headline FY27 EPS guide will compare against a FY26 base about $0.19 inflated (about $3.00-3.10 excluding refunds vs $3.19-3.29 reported), which risks a 'down-year' headline even at a flat underlying guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EPS included $0.11 of refunds and the stock still fell 2.92%. Refunds have not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell side models refunds explicitly, so this is mostly priced. What is left is the headline optics of the year-over-year comparison.

findings.finding: The November 2025 restructuring targets about $1B of gross run-rate savings by end of FY28 (4,000-6,000 roles, $650M of charges, about $250M of them in FY26). That gives FY27 a mid-programme cost tailwind HP can put in the guide against memory costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announced with the soft FY26 guide in Nov 2025 (-1.4%). It did not offset the guide then.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a year and in models, so it is mostly priced. The only unpriced part is how much FY27 phasing the interim team discloses.

outside_window.finding: Emma Walmsley takes over as CEO on 2027-01-04. A strategic review or a reset of the FY27 frame under the new CEO would land at the Q1 FY27 print (late Feb 2027) or at an analyst day, not in this window.

baseline_tension: The evidence is mixed and nets slightly negative. The negative half (units, channel inventory, the 2027 unit outlook, the CEO transition, the Xerox print read) agrees with the +7.6 put skew and the -15% 20-day slide, so it is probably largely priced. The positive half (peer margins, memory slowdown, beat habit, an over-hedged tape) cuts against them. That keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (beats sold: last two prints -2.92% and -1.88% after guide-topping EPS): the beat-pattern finding went from +0.8 to +0.4.
Lesson 6 (the FY27 bar is stale and single-sourced): guidance findings were capped small. Memory slowdown went from +0.8 to +0.6 and channel inventory from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 5 (third-party unit proxy, not HP's own number; HP prioritises profitable units, so this is a revenue-not-EPS risk): the IDC unit finding went from -1.0 to -0.7.

Lesson 7 (positive sign against a +7.6 skew; the 'no cause for the drawdown' argument is weak evidence): the positioning finding went from +1.0 to +0.6. The negatives agree with the skew, so they were left at their already-small sizes rather than cut twice.
CEO-transition inference went from -0.4 to -0.3 (inference, largely priced via the elevated implied move). The tariff roll-off went from -0.2 to -0.1 (a one-off with no path to the operating guide).
Lesson 8 / core (understatement is the systematic error; this is a first FY27 guide): abs_move went from 7.5 to 8.0. p_up stayed at 49 because the evidence is balanced.
Left standing: the peer-margin finding (+0.6, a peer print after HP last spoke, documents), the 2027 unit assumption (-0.6), Xerox (-0.3) and restructuring (+0.2).
